text:
incident-bot: P1 alert: us-west-2 GPU capacity spiral detected. Autoscaler failing to recover, high queue growth, driver Xid/OOM errors. Paging oncall.

alex: seeing large queue spikes across inference service A. queue length ~2400 -> 5400 in 5m. autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions, all failed with driver errors.

tamika: confirmed. host-level logs show repeated CUDA Xid 13 and kernel OOMs on several nodes. looks like driver rollout yesterday might be correlated.

liam: @alex can you drop the autoscaler events? I see `Reached max_replicas=12` then `scale rejected: node-group capacity error`.

alex: pasted autoscaler log ->
```
2026-03-15T02:09:12Z autoscaler: scale up from 6 to 9
2026-03-15T02:09:14Z k8s: provisioning request accepted
2026-03-15T02:09:58Z driver: Xid 13 on /dev/nvidia0
2026-03-15T02:10:01Z node: kernel OOM, process nvidia-driver
2026-03-15T02:10:05Z autoscaler: provisioning failed: driver boot verification failed
2026-03-15T02:11:40Z autoscaler: reached policy max_replicas=12
```
kevin: so autoscaler is blocked because newly provisioned nodes fail driver checks => capacity stuck. Need fallback plan.

ops-runbook: recommend immediate steps:
1) disable new driver rollout (if still queued)
2) drain nodes showing Xid/OOM
3) route critical traffic to reserved on-demand pool (dedicated)
4) temporarily raise per-customer rate limits to reduce queue growth

tamika: starting step 2. cordoning nodes with repeated Xid. running `kubectl cordon <node>` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` now.

alex: started traffic-shift to fallback pool via routing rule: set route weight inference-service A -> fallback: 60%. will monitor latencies.

customer-success: flagging that several big customers saw increased 5xx rates starting ~02:10 PDT. estimating 6-8 customers with visible impact; one enterprise had ~40% failure until routing change. notifying CSMs.

oncall-l2: taking over paging at 02:18 UTC. handing from alex -> tamika. tamika is primary. status: queue rising but growth rate slowed after routing change.

liam: noticed autoscaler is also throttled by quota: `quotaExceeded: GPUs 0/20 available` in cloud provider responses. there are both driver failures and quota exhaustion preventing new capacity.

kevin: quick mitigation: 1) ask cloud infra to temporarily increase GPU quota (contacted via slack channel cloud-ops), 2) rollback driver to previous stable build in parallel.

tamika: rollback started: releasing driver v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0 on a canary set. monitoring for Xid reduction.

incident-bot: Note: created incident CR on tracker #INC-2026-0315-42. runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/inc-2026-0315-42

alex: also enabling KV cache to reduce repeated warm token generation to shave load. small config push to all services applied.

ops-runbook: throttles applied: temporary per-customer QPS caps + longer client-side backoff recommended. document in runbook.

tamika: driver rollback canary nodes now back to stable and reporting fewer Xid/OOM. 3 of 4 canary apps green. holding until 02:28 to expand.

liam: quota increase approved (temporary) -> cloud-ops: +10 GPUs, new quota available. will allow autoscaler to add nodes once driver issue cleared.

kevin: after expanding the rollback and enabling fallback pool, queue now trending down: 5400 -> 1800 over 20m. request failure rates down to ~8% cluster-wide.

customer-success: CSM update posted. some customers will need post-incident follow-up. marking those with highest error rates.

oncall-l2: performing handoff notes for next shift: steps taken, current mitigations, rollback status, quota increase, customer impact summary. handing to kevin at 02:40 UTC.

kevin: I'll monitor through the hour and coordinate permanent remediation: revert driver rollout pipeline, add preflight boot checks, and add autoscaler tolerance when provisioning failures occur.

alex: preliminary impact assessment: ~9 customers affected, median 5xx spike 10-25%, peak 40% for one enterprise, estimated 4k failed requests over the window.

tamika: follow-ups: root-cause: driver rollout exposed stability regression causing node boot validation to fail -> autoscaler plus quota constraints amplified capacity loss -> queue spiral. next: add circuit-breaker to route traffic earlier to fallback pools and improve autoscaler backoff and retry visibility.

incident-bot: incident moved to status: mitigated -> monitoring. timeline added to #INC-2026-0315-42.

customer-success: will coordinate customer comms draft for postmortem.

kevin: closing loop: expand driver rollback completion at 03:05 UTC, autoscaler able to add nodes, queue back to baseline ~300, SLA errors under threshold. please add action items to the postmortem.

oncall-l2: final handover: incident resolved -> monitoring. signing off at 02:53 UTC. :white_check_mark:
